newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechen leader injured in car accident -- agency.
newsitem.headline: Chechen leader injured in car accident -- agency.

text.p: Chechen separatist leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev was taken to hospital with broken arm after a car accident in the regional capital Grozny on Thursday, Itar-Tass news agency said.

The agency quoted deputy premier in the separatist government, Movladi Udugov, as saying that the accident which had taken place in Grozny was not deliberate and ruled out any possibility of a terrorist act.
Udugov said there was not threat to Yandarbiyev's life and that the rebel leader was in good shape.

Yandarbiyev is preparing to stand in the election scheduled for January 27 for leader of the Caucasus region in southern Russia. Another 18 candidates, including all notable rebel figures, will also take part in the polls.

The rebels called the elections after they struck a peace deal with Russia under which Moscow agreed to withdraw its forces sent to the southern region in December 1994 to quell its three-year independence bid.

The rebels agreed under the August 31 deal to postpone by five years the decision on Chechnya's future political status. They make little secret of the fact that they want full independence -- a demand that Moscow rejects outright.
